newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sets special contract for spring harvest grain.
newsitem.headline: CWB sets special contract for spring harvest grain.

text.p: A special delivery contract was announced on Thursday for farmers who were not able to harvest wheat and barley before snow fell on the Prairies in October, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
The early and heavy snowfall stopped harvest operations on the western Prairies with four percent of grains and oilseeds remaining on the fields, Agriculture Canada said in November.
United Grain Growers Ltd said five percent of crops were not harvested in Alberta and Saskatchewan and three percent were not threshed in Manitoba.
The CWB announced its special Series U contract Thursday.

The contract applies to Canada Western Feed Wheat, Canada Western Feed Wheat sample account light weight, No5 Canada Western Amber Durum wheat and Extra No1 as well as Extra No1 and No2 Canada Western Barley, the CWB said.
"Any other grades offered under this program must be authorized by CWB area representatives," the CWB said.
Series U contracts must be signed no later than June 6, 1997, the CWB said.

Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale in November approved emergency funds for wheat and barley growers not able to harvest in the fall. The action, termed the Prairie Grain Advance Payments Act, allowed payments of up to C$15,000 a farmer for unharvested grain and C$3,000 to dry grain.
